brief: The town is empty after dark, so #51's going-home mechanism fires under once a night. Give the night its own arrival source: `spawnHomeAgent()` sends a walker in from a lane edge after `nightF > 0.3` who walks straight to an unused `HOME_DOORS` entry whose `windowHours()` says somebody is home tonight and whose priced `pathHours()` arrival fits before `HOME_MIN` of the dawn edge, then goes in through `arriveHome()` so the window over that door lights the frame they enter. Model it on `spawnTapAgent`: its own rate and its own presence bound (at most two on the way at once), excluded from the count `scarcity` reads, never a share of `laneCap`. Also fix c87 while you are in `drawFaceRow`: a row-64 pane over a home door is drawn live and then night-tinted, so it lands at half the warmth of a cached pane — a window someone just came home to must read as warm as the rest.
successLooksLike: Over ten seed-nights `probes/going-home.mjs` counts 3–5 arrivals a night (from under 1), every one inside its window's hours, and `windows-night.mjs` total lit counts stay within noise of HEAD because the register only moves WHEN a window lights, not whether. A midnight wide shot shows a figure on the lane walking toward a door; the pane over it goes from dark to full warmth the frame they vanish.
avoid: Do not widen laneCap or let these walkers take lane itineraries — they are going home, one leg, no stops. Do not change windowHours()'s hash or the 0.15–2 h dusk offsets; the register is the only thing that moves. Expect census churn from the new R() draws: replay over ten seeds, read for collapse only.
